name: POSCO
verdict: POSCO's group held 70% of two joint ventures with MEHL, the Myanmar military's conglomerate, which a UN fact-finding mission said help fund the military.
note: Front (chest) sponsor of Pohang Steelers' 2026 home kit: the chest block reads posco over FANTASTEEL, POSCO's ad campaign (claim posco-fantasteel, The Korea Herald, 2023-12-25), with '환동해중심 포항' underneath — all in the club store's 2026 home-shirt product renders and the K League's 2026-02-10 kit-launch photo ('FC POHANG STEELERS 2026 League Kits'). Rating note: concern (maintainer decision, 1 Oct 2026, #919; METHOD.md: a joint venture with a military's conglomerate that a UN body documents counts). POSCO is a 100% subsidiary of POSCO Holdings; South Korea's National Pension Service holds 8.30% of POSCO Holdings (posco-holdings-shareholders), which isn't a link (METHOD.md). Also found in review, not used for the rating: Amnesty International's 5 July 2013 press release on forced evictions and a police baton charge over land for the POSCO-India steel project in Odisha (https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/press-release/2013/07/india-victims-forced-evictions-odisha-must-receive-effective-remedy-and-rep/).

why.text: A UN fact-finding mission on Myanmar named two joint ventures that POSCO companies hold 70% of with MEHL, the Myanmar military's business conglomerate, and found that foreign partners in such ventures at a minimum help fund the military. Amnesty International also named POSCO among MEHL's partners. POSCO's affiliate POSCO C&C said in 2021 it would end its venture with MEHL.
why.messageLine: A UN fact-finding mission named POSCO's joint ventures with the Myanmar military's conglomerate, MEHL, among business ties that help fund the military.
